NICHESv2: Spatial Cell-to-Cell Ligand-Receptor Communication Analysis

Source: R/NICHESv2-package.R
NICHESv2-package.Rd

NICHESv2 computes ligand-receptor (LR) signaling scores between pairs of cells in spatial and non-spatial single-cell transcriptomics data. It improves on the original NICHES package with:

  • A memory-efficient long-format output object (NICHESObject, 15 slots).

  • Support for multi-gene ligand and receptor complexes (underscore-delimited, e.g. "COL1A1_COL1A2").

  • Built-in loaders for the ConnectomeDB2025 (default), FANTOM5, and OmniPath LR databases.

  • Per-edge and per-cell normalized scores alongside raw counts.

  • Parallel LR computation via socket clusters on all platforms.

  • Flexible aggregation (aggregate_NICHESObject).

Typical workflow


library(NICHESv2)

# 1. Load / prepare inputs
#    count.mtx : gene x cell sparse matrix  (rownames = genes, colnames = cells)
#    meta.data : data.frame                  (rownames = cells; spatial mode
#                                             needs "x" and "y" columns)
#    LRM.db    : "connectomedb2025" | "fantom5" | "omnipath" | user data.frame

# 2. Build the NICHESObject (one call does everything)
niches.obj <- create_NICHESObject(
  count.mtx = count.mtx,
  meta.data = meta.data,
  LRM.db    = "connectomedb2025",
  k         = 6L,           # 6-nearest-neighbor graph
  method    = "product"
)

# 3. Inspect
print(niches.obj)
summary(niches.obj)
dim(niches.obj)            # cells / genes / edges / LRMs

# 4. Aggregate neighborhood edge signals
niches.obj <- aggregate_NICHESObject(niches.obj, cell.type.col = "celltype")

# 5. Subset to a cell population (aggregation rows carry over unchanged)
b.cells <- niches.obj$cell.meta[celltype == "B_cell", cell]
sub.obj  <- niches.obj[b.cells]

NICHESObject slot reference

SlotTypeContents
$cell.listcharacterCell barcodes
$cell.datadata.table(cell, gene, score, score.norm) – sparse
$cell.metadata.tablePer-cell metadata (x, y, celltype, ...)
$edge.listdata.table(edge, SendingCell, ReceivingCell)
$edge.datadata.table(edge, LRM, score, score.norm) – sparse
$edge.metadata.tablePer-edge metadata with Sending/Receiving/Joint cols
$neighborhood.cell.listlistPer-cell neighbor barcodes
$neighborhood.edge.listlistPer-cell neighborhood edge IDs
$neighborhood.metadata.table(cell, n.neighbors, n.edges)
$gene.listcharacterGene names
$gene.metadata.tablePer-gene annotation
$LRM.listcharacter"ligand|receptor" strings
$LRM.metadata.tablePer-LRM annotation (pathway, class, ...)
$segmentationsf or NULLOptional cell polygons
$aggregationslistAggregation tables computed on demand

Key separators

  • Edge IDs: "SendingCell|ReceivingCell"

  • LRM IDs: "ligand|receptor"

  • Gene complexes in database: "gene1_gene2" (underscore)

Key naming conventions

  • Function names use underscores: create_NICHESObject()

  • Variable / argument names use dots: n.cores, bg.color

  • Score columns: score (raw), score.norm (normalized)

References

Ramilowski, J.A. et al. (2015). A draft network of ligand-receptor-mediated multicellular signalling in human. Nature Communications, 6, 7866.

Turei, D. et al. (2021). Integrated intra- and intercellular signaling knowledge for multicellular omics analysis. Molecular Systems Biology, 17(3), e9923.
